Mirror, reflection blur, panorama rotation, flat-image warp, edge tint, saturation, samples, film thickness/variation, light colour, faces, flip V, teaching stages. Audit round 2 added Energy conserving (off by default, so presets are unchanged), Colour parameters (Auto follows the project's colour space) and Demo render.
Universality first (any object, scene, camera, least wiring), then the match to the four reference images (look, not shape).

C1 Refraction TOP alpha, C2 picking and colour buffers, C3 fan-gap dispersion only if measured better, C4 no dithering, C5 numeric and diagnostic hardening, C6 measured screen orientation, C7 fog, C8 Object size with Fit to Glass geometry, C9 comparable demo backdrops; not the negative back-face encoding, footprintLod, two-surface optics, scene lights or the flow vertex stage.
Rejected: the fan-gap mip level doubled the error against 64- and 128-sample references (decisions.json).

The orientation is measured by comparing the pixel's projected position with its raster position, not with dFdx/dFdy as in Prism: derivatives misread a few silhouette pixels (up to 50/255 against the old image).

answers.quote: Flip V stays as the UV-only override.
answers.value: Flip V flips the base UV and the measured vertical direction together. With a measured direction, a UV-only Flip V breaks both cases Flip V exists for, including the round-1 case (about 72,000 wrong pixels in the preview); flipping both gives the round-1 result exactly and also fixes upside-down inputs in a normal raster. Revisit if the user prefers the literal wording.

Object size is relative to the demo torus the presets were tuned on (1 = the same size, 1.45 units in radius), so Fit on the demo gives exactly 1; Fit multiplies the SOP's half size by the Geometry COMP's world scale. One control cannot keep both the bend (scene units) and the ripples (on the SOP) right for a scaled Geometry COMP while Object size 1 changes nothing; the ripple side is documented.
Backdrop is a Study control that experiments reset (their predictions describe the checkerboard); Object size is a setup control that nothing resets.

The Liquid Glass Blobs formula as is; the variant that subtracts the destination was not adopted (it assumes the Refraction TOP is exactly the image the glass is drawn over). Partly covered pixels count the scene twice (documented limit).

answers.topic: family sync fix V1: transparent scenes with the back-face pass
answers.value: Supplied: the user's priority (universality first) and the verifier's preferred fix. Inferred: take the fix, not the documented limit. Where the back-face pass covers the view, the colour comes from it and the coverage from the Refraction TOP's alpha at the same spot, so a transparent scene stays transparent with the pass on, and opaque scenes render exactly as before. Not adopted: storing coverage in the back-face pass (its alpha holds the distance; another channel or a sign encoding would need a native check).

added_controls_family_sync: Inputs > Object size and Fit to Glass geometry; Study > Backdrop. Glass geometry now also feeds Fit.
open_questions: Family critic: should Object size switch to SOP units, with the shader following the Geometry COMP's scale and each instance's scale by itself (decisions.json, Family critic: one Object size per component, option (b))? It would make animated and per-instance scale work without Fit, but changes what a typed Object size means on a scaled COMP, in every member.

Family open question (centre-line residual): with antialiasing, a few silhouette pixels near the render's centre row or column still take the wrong screen orientation, so they bend the wrong way. In the WebGL preview each member's survey finds up to 8 of them per row of twelve renders; in the final image they change at most 7 pixels per row, by up to 43/255 in an emulated flipped raster and up to 38/255 in TouchDesigner's usual one. Are they visible in TouchDesigner? The native check centre_line_residual (validation.json, family_close.native_run) answers it. If they are, try a centroid-qualified vertex output for the projected position in Liquid Glass Lit first (form (e) of Lit's survey), then bring it to the core and the other members. Until then no member changes its shader for it.
